findings.spec: FR-8 (webhook strips punctuation and spaces and matches opt-out phrases itself); Flow 2 step 4
findings.summary: isOptOutMessage missed keywords split by a space or punctuation inside a longer message ('un-subscribe me', 'please s-t-o-p texting', 're-voke consent', 'can-cel please'); Twilio's filter misses them too, so the customer stayed opted in.
findings.evidence: Failing vitest cases on main and at c7c74dd; 6 new tests fail before the fix, pass after.

findings.summary: locations.sms_number has no DB check for E.164 (SPEC data model says E.164, unique). A non-E.164 value would make inbound STOP fall back to platform-wide suppression only (still blocks all sends). No code writes sms_number yet (FR-1 not built); enforce when FR-1 lands.

sheet_sources.attestation_id FK is not tenant-scoped (customers' attestation FK is). importRows rejects a foreign-business attestation at runtime (every row 'attestation_invalid'), so no wrong consent is stored; consider a tenant-scoped FK or a not_configured result.

Reliability line 316 says sheet reads 'track the last row ID so a row is never imported twice'; implementation re-reads the whole sheet and dedups by row ID in visits, keeping last_row_id as a progress marker only. Meets the intent (never imported twice, tested incl. crash/concurrency); PR #2 already lists rewording line 316 as a Doc follow-up.

SPEC does not say how sheet row IDs are generated or whether they are stable. A template that reuses IDs (e.g. =ROW() after deleting a row) or re-pointing a location to a new sheet would make new rows skip as duplicate_visit. Recommend the SPEC/template require stable, never-reused row IDs.
